label: FS AP-T565 (Wi-Fi 6 outdoor AP, copper + fibre)
description: FS AP-T565 - Wi-Fi 6 (802.11ax) IP68 outdoor AP, 2x2 dual-radio, 1x 1G RJ45 with 802.3af PoE-in (12.95 W max), 1x 1G SFP, 1x RJ45 console.
notes: Vendor figures from the FS AP-T565 datasheet, product characteristics table: Service Port **1x 10/100/1000Base-T Ethernet port, 1x 1G SFP port**; Management Port **1x RJ45 Console port**; Power Supply **IEEE 802.3af PoE, DC 48V/0.35A**; Power Consumption **<12.95 W**; radios **2.4G/5G 2x2 MIMO**, maximum access rate **2.402 Gbps** (single radio) and **1.775 Gbps in 2.4G+5G mode**, which is the 574M + 1.2G pair modelled here. FS's product page (https://www.fs.com/products/149657.html) repeats it: 'one SFP interface and one 10/100/1000M interface with PoE/local power supply', Power-over-Ethernet **802.3af**, PoE injector sold separately. This supersedes the previous version of this file, which cited https://resource.fs.com/mall/file/datasheet/ap-w6d1775c-access-point-datasheet.pdf - an **indoor** Wi-Fi 6 AP with five copper jacks - and so gave the T565 five Ethernet ports and a PoE+ PSE on eth4. The T565 datasheet has no PSE at all: its single RJ45 jack is the PoE **inlet**, 802.3af only, which is why nothing here sources power. The console port is recorded here rather than as an interface because it carries no frames.
